alignments.note: Anarthrous Greek, so the supplied determiner is an ordinary rule 7/51 helper on the noun.

One Greek compound noun expanded to *men that speak lies*; rule 91 heads on the word glossing the lexeme, *speak*, as `βλασφημοῦντες` → *speaking evil of* heads on *speaking*, with *men* the generic completion and *of* the case preposition riding along.
The whole supplied expansion *as with a hot iron* belongs to the participle, no other source token licensing it; discontinuous under rule 15.
Rule 47: `ἴδιος` between article and expressed noun carries the supplied possessive, so the article realizes nothing.
Rule 47: *their own* to the possessive adjective.
The article being unrepresented, the supplied case preposition stays with the noun (rule 21's determinerless clause); discontinuous under rule 15.

review_notes: The head of `ψευδολόγων` was reviewed independently: *men* is the generic completion and *speak* the gloss, so rule 91's operational test puts the head there rather than on the formal English noun.
